learningObjective: Understand the online softmax recurrence: running max + rescale of running sum on each new tile.

canonicalClaims.claim: The online softmax recurrence for tile-wise processing is: `m = max(m_prev, m_new)`, `s = s_prev * exp(m_prev - m) + s_new * exp(m_new - m)`. This is an exact algebraic identity ensuring that after all tiles are processed, `s = sum_i exp(x_i - m)` with `m = max_i x_i`.
conditions: Tile-wise processing; sufficient FP precision (typically FP32).
nonImplications: Does not imply bit-associativity; different tile orders give different rounding.
Does not imply the recurrence is FlashAttention-specific; it applies to any tile-wise softmax.

misconceptions.claim: The recurrence is simple addition: `m = m_prev + m_new`, `s = s_prev + s_new`.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Fails to rescale sums to the new max anchor.

misconceptions.claim: The running max never updates after the first tile.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Fails when later tiles contain a larger max.

misconceptions.claim: The recurrence only works in FP16.
misconceptions.whyWrong: FP32 works fine and is the standard choice.
It is exact algebra of the softmax denominator.

implementationFacts: Also used as the core of FlashAttention's numerator recurrence via `l * exp(m_prev - m)` rescaling.
Well-conditioned when `m` stays finite; -inf initial max is safe (contributes zero).
